title: Soil
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 2 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child identifies sand, clay and loam and classifies them by the ribbon test and particle size.

floor.question: What happens to soil when you add water?

board.do: Draw three ribbons: long, short, broken.
Wait for the child to say clay.
Label each ribbon with its soil.

misconceptions.ask: How can you tell clay from sand?
misconceptions.repair: Give two soils of the same colour that feel different. Do the ribbon test.

misconceptions.ask: Which soil makes the longest ribbon?
misconceptions.repair: Roll wet sand and wet clay. Sand breaks; clay stretches.

listen_for: Clay, it is in big lumps
misconceptions.ask: Which soil has the biggest particles?
misconceptions.repair: Rub each soil between the fingers and look with a hand lens. Sand grains are big and seen.
Show three samples side by side and name each. Mud is wet soil of any type.

checks.question: Which soil falls apart and makes no ribbon?
Name the three types of soil.
